title: Prim's minimum spanning tree
summary: Grow one tree from a start vertex, always adding the cheapest edge that reaches a new vertex.

checkpoints.text: A minimum spanning tree connects every vertex using the cheapest set of edges. `key` (under each vertex) is the cheapest edge found so far that would bring the vertex into the tree.
From 0, vertex 2 can join for 1 and vertex 1 for 4.
The cheapest key belongs to vertex 2 (1), so edge 0 – 2 joins the tree.
Through 2, vertex 1 can now join for 2, cheaper than 4. Its key and parent change.
Tree edges 2 - 1, 0 - 2, 1 - 3, 3 - 4, total weight 11. Prim is like Dijkstra, but `key` holds the cost of one edge instead of a whole path. O(V²) with a matrix scan.
